differences.what: The actual new candidate shows one low Wolf gable with a dark door and small right sash, its long roof receding left. The other gable ends near source x32, outside the physical engraving art edge near x40; no mesh part, source crop or renderer mask was hidden. The old frame exposing an extra outward door is superseded only for this framing question.

Held-out door head residual is 20.549 px, 46.763 px per native metre, conditionally 0.439 m. Adding existing 12 px camera/roof and 8 px held-out pick envelopes gives 0.012–0.867 m before camera-family uncertainty. This does not establish a visitor-visible >0.3 m construction defect. Keep door geometry; this corrects the earlier overstrong open-door visual note.

Current sign head z=10.3 m is an explicit reconstructed pose governed by NYPL, whose conditional 9.743–10.557 m pixel-envelope interval contains it. Hammon gives 6.991–8.409 m and the two Colbert cameras give materially different intervals (8.962–9.980 and 8.080–8.939 m). These inversions hold native XY and provisional camera fixed and are not surveys or statistical confidence intervals. Conflicting drawings/camera families warrant within tolerance under T-3153; no universal pole delta is supported.

The single-gable fit has unchanged manual uncertainty 12 px and max residual 11.054 px. The late engraved roof hatching and source-specific roof-edge/stack projection are not measurements of historic reflectance or a consistent missing element against NYPL.

Neutral single-anchor photo_match does not show the application roof normal/ORM treatment, terrain, riverbank, trees, figures, neighbours or authentic historic pigment. Those absent scene elements do not validate app finish or surveyed placement.

The illustration is retrospective and depicts its stated earlier date. Exact 5 m compartments, plan, dimensions, hidden fabric and metric sign pose remain reconstructed; unchanged appearance on 1 July 1835 is not directly attested.
